memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Kara rejected a double-bed-only St. Louis hotel for the teaching weekend, kept Hampton Forest Park as the practical hold despite no hot tub, and set the Sunday return search for 6:15 p.m. or later with 7:05 preferred over 5:40.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: I don't want doubles for that weekend.

messages.content: St. Louis update: Sunday lab is confirmed until 2:30, then about 20-30 minutes teardown. Host list came in. Closest hotel is attached to the clinic garage, but reviews are weaker and the room type only shows two doubles. Hampton/Forest Park is about 12 minutes out with a queen, coffee, mini-fridge, pool and fitness, no hot tub. Can you rerank and tell me what Sunday return times are safe?

I’d rank by least-risk, not distance: 1) Hampton Forest Park — best room basics and better feedback; commute is the variable. 2) Attached-garage hotel — only wins for Friday loading, and not with double beds. 3) Drury/other Forest Park option — recovery backup. For flights, before 5:30 is too tight. 5:45-6:15 works only with a staged ride/light teardown. After 6:15, especially 7-ish, is the safe band.
Host says Friday setup is 4:30 and I can load through that garage. Does that push the attached one up?

A little, but not past Hampton. The garage hotel solves one setup hassle and creates two stay risks: weaker guest feedback and double beds unless they confirm otherwise. For three nights before teaching, I’d only use it if the queen room exists and the rate is refundable.
Agreed. I don't want doubles for that weekend.

Then filter it out unless they confirm a single queen or king. Hampton stays first: refundable Thu-Sun, quiet queen room requested, coffee/fridge verified, pool and fitness listed. Caveat to note: no hot tub, and Friday drive time needs a buffer.
For flights, I found a 5:40 STL departure and a 7:05. Both connect.

Pick 7:05. The 5:40 asks you to leave campus by about 3:15, which assumes perfect teardown and no security line. The 7:05 gives time to finish, get to STL without rushing, and still avoids a brutal late-night departure.
Okay, hold Hampton through Sunday and search returns at 6:15 or later. If Monday becomes necessary, flag it but don't book it.

Done. Working plan: refundable Hampton Forest Park queen-room hold for Jul 24-27. Attached-garage hotel is out unless it confirms a single queen/king and better terms. Return search starts at 6:15 p.m.; 7:05 beats 5:40. Monday stays alert-only, not booked.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Kara kept the Denver reservations after the airline moved the return earlier. The 12:45 p.m. DEN departure remains workable if she leaves the optional breakfast around 9:00, and the pool closure is noted as a downgrade but not enough to change hotels because the fitness room and room setup remain intact.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: the room still has the coffee maker and kitchenette/fridge
The pool closure is what irritates me. Worth switching convention-center hotels this late?

messages.content: Denver wrinkle: United moved my Sunday return 70 minutes earlier, so DEN is now 12:45 p.m. The app moved badge pickup to the Welton/14th entrance. Homewood also says the pool will be closed for resurfacing, but fitness room is open and the room still has the coffee maker and kitchenette/fridge. Keep or scramble?

I’d keep it unless the Sunday breakfast is a must past 9:30 or the pool was central. For a 12:45 departure, aim to be at DEN around 10:45. That means leaving the hotel roughly 9:45-10:00. The new badge entrance is annoying for arrival logistics, but it does not break the return if bags are at the hotel and you are not checking luggage.
Educator breakfast is 7:30 to 9:00, optional but useful. No checked bag. I just don't want a sprint.

That still works. Leave breakfast at 8:55, walk back, grab bags/check out by about 9:25, and call the car by 9:35. Even with a 45-55 minute airport ride, you should have a normal buffer. If the session runs long, leave before the closing announcements.
The pool closure is what irritates me. Worth switching convention-center hotels this late?

I would not switch just for that. It is a real downgrade from the booking, but the fitness room and room setup remain intact. One week out, a change risks higher rates, worse cancellation terms, or losing the kitchenette/fridge. I’d only move if another nearby hotel is refundable, similarly rated, and explicitly confirms pool plus the room basics.
Okay. Keep it, then?

Yes. Keep the United change and the Homewood reservation. Caveats: skip or leave the breakfast early if timing slips; use the new badge entrance on arrival day, not as a Sunday route; confirm pool closure in writing in case they offer points or a small adjustment; and recheck seats after the schedule change, especially that final leg where the window was not worth the fee.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Kara opened a late-August Blue Ridge partner trip around a Bent Creek trail event. She prioritized practical timing, avoiding an exhausting arrival, recovery facilities, and confirmed room basics over the cheapest route. Flying is favored over the full drive, with GSP and AVL preferred before CLT; for this partner trip adjacent seats matter more than a window.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Recovery matters. I found a downtown inn, 4.6, walkable, but no real pool/hot tub and maybe tiny gym. Mountain lodge near Arden is 4.2, pool, hot tub, fitness, but I can't tell if rooms have coffee or a fridge.
but I can't tell if rooms have coffee or a fridge
Room setup: one bed is fine. Queen is enough; king is not necessary. If the lodge only has doubles, skip it.
For seats, adjacent matters more than window; if we can get window-aisle together, great, but don't split us.

messages.content: Now that Denver is mostly handled, I want to start the Blue Ridge weekend. Late August, Saturday trail event near Asheville, Sunday recovery day, home Monday. Sam and I can leave Tampa Friday morning or maybe early afternoon. I need drive-versus-fly by practicality, not just cheapest.
Sure. To compare this cleanly, what is the event area, start time, gear, and do you want the hotel base closer to trails, downtown food, or recovery amenities?

Event is at Bent Creek, 8:30 Saturday. Two of us, trail shoes and poles, no bikes. Recovery matters. I found a downtown inn, 4.6, walkable, but no real pool/hot tub and maybe tiny gym. Mountain lodge near Arden is 4.2, pool, hot tub, fitness, but I can't tell if rooms have coffee or a fridge.

First read: driving Tampa-Asheville is reliable but costs most of Friday and Monday. Flying into Asheville is best if fares/times are sane. Greenville-Spartanburg is the practical backup, about 75-90 minutes by car. Charlotte gives more flight choice but about two hours of rental-car driving. Atlanta is only worth it if everything else is terrible.
Don't make this a cheapest-wins thing. I don't want to arrive wrecked Friday night or waste all of Monday. Friday morning is possible, early afternoon if my Friday patient call runs long.

Then full driving is the backup plan, not the baseline. A Friday afternoon road departure gets you in very late. For flights, target arrival by midafternoon: AVL/GSP by 2:30, CLT by 1:00. Monday return should probably leave early-to-mid afternoon so you are not rushing out of a recovery morning.
Does CLT defeat the purpose? Sam found more options there.

Not if the arrival is early. CLT plus the two-hour drive still saves several hours over the full road trip and has more airline choices. But if the only affordable CLT option lands after 4:00, it becomes a long evening after travel. GSP is the better compromise if fares are close.
Hotel base is the part I'm stuck on. Downtown sounds nicer for Sunday food, but after Bent Creek, hot tub may be more useful. I don't want a no-fridge surprise.

For this trip, I’d lean mountain/Arden if the room basics confirm. It is easier for Bent Creek and gives you pool, hot tub, and fitness access for Sunday. The downtown inn wins on walkable restaurants and stronger rating, but it is a weaker recovery setup. Missing fridge/coffee at the lodge would be the caveat that could flip the choice.
Can you give me a compact shortlist I can send Sam? Include driving, even if it's a backup.

Practicality shortlist: 1) Fly TPA-GSP, rent car, stay Arden lodge — best balance if flight times are decent. 2) Fly TPA-AVL — shortest ground transfer, but only if price and schedule are not ugly. 3) Fly TPA-CLT — useful if it saves money or gives better nonstop/connection timing, but avoid late arrival. 4) Drive Tampa-Asheville — cheapest-feeling and gear-easy, but burns both travel days.
Sam worries about rental car pickup and mountain roads after dark. Which airport avoids that best?

AVL avoids it best. GSP is next; the drive is straightforward if you land by midafternoon. CLT is okay only with an early arrival and a prebooked rental. I would not plan ATL for this unless it is a huge fare difference and you are both fine with a long drive.
Room setup: one bed is fine. Queen is enough; king is not necessary. If the lodge only has doubles, skip it.

Good. For the lodge I’d verify: one queen or king, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge or refrigerator, pool/hot tub hours, fitness access, parking, and cancellation terms. If they cannot confirm the fridge or coffee, hold the downtown inn instead and accept that recovery facilities are limited.
The lodge listing says select rooms with refrigerators. That makes me nervous.

Reasonable. Do not book a mystery room there. Ask for the exact room category with refrigerator in writing, or book by phone and have them add it to the reservation. If they will only note a request, I’d treat downtown as more reliable.
Which one would you hold tonight?

Hold the Arden lodge only if it is refundable and they confirm a single queen/king plus fridge and coffee. That base fits the trail event and Sunday recovery better. If confirmation is vague, hold the downtown inn as the safe-room backup, then revisit once the event packet gives parking and packet-pickup details.

Let's do that. Search flights GSP first, AVL if times are surprisingly good, CLT only if it saves a lot without landing late. No airfare until we see the event packet. For seats, adjacent matters more than window; if we can get window-aisle together, great, but don't split us.

Plan set: try a refundable Arden lodge hold with the exact room basics confirmed; downtown inn is the backup if the lodge cannot guarantee them. Flight search order will be GSP, then AVL, then CLT only with an early enough arrival and meaningful savings; Monday returns in the afternoon. I will leave airfare unbooked until the event packet, and for this partner trip I’ll prioritize adjacent seats over chasing a window.
